rules.title: Runtime.exec() with a built command string
rules.description: The single-string form of exec() is split on whitespace and, on some platforms, handed to a shell. A concatenated command lets the caller add arguments or commands.
rules.remediation: Use the String[] overload, or ProcessBuilder with an explicit argument list.

rules.title: JDBC statement built by concatenation
rules.description: Statement, unlike PreparedStatement, sends the SQL text exactly as assembled. Concatenating a value into it is injection.
rules.remediation: Use PreparedStatement with ? placeholders and setX() binding.
examples: stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = " + id);

rules.title: Spring expression parsed from a runtime string
rules.description: SpEL evaluates against the application context and can reach arbitrary beans and, through them, arbitrary code.
rules.remediation: Never parse an expression built from input. Use a fixed template with a restricted EvaluationContext if you must.

rules.title: TrustManager that accepts every certificate
rules.description: An empty checkServerTrusted, or a hostname verifier that always returns true, removes TLS authentication entirely.
rules.remediation: Use the platform trust store. For an internal CA, load it into a KeyStore rather than disabling verification.
examples: public void checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[] chain, String authType) {}

rules.title: XML factory created without disabling DTDs
rules.description: Java's XML factories resolve external entities by default, so a crafted document reads local files and makes outbound requests as the server.
rules.remediation: Set the feature http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl to true immediately after newInstance().

rules.title: Cipher.getInstance with a weak transformation
rules.description: The transformation string names a broken cipher or an unauthenticated mode. AES with no mode defaults to ECB.
rules.remediation: Use "AES/GCM/NoPadding" with a unique 12-byte nonce per message.

rules.title: Spring Security rule permits everything
rules.description: A permitAll on /** makes every later rule unreachable - Spring evaluates matchers in order and the first match wins.
rules.remediation: Order matchers most-specific first and end with anyRequest().authenticated().

rules.title: Spring Security CSRF protection disabled
rules.description: Disabling CSRF on a cookie-authenticated application lets a third-party page make state-changing requests as the logged-in user.
rules.remediation: Keep CSRF on. For a stateless token API, it is genuinely unnecessary - document that the app never authenticates by cookie.
